text:
Both integrate changes from one branch into another. Different history shape.

## Merge

```
main:    A─B─C───────M
feature:      D─E─F─╯
```

Creates new "merge commit" M. Both branch histories preserved. Easy to see where branch started/ended.

**Use when:**
- Working on shared/public branches
- Want honest history ("this was a feature branch")
- Collaborating — others may have cloned your branch

**Tradeoffs:**
- ✅ Safe, non-destructive
- ✅ Conflict once at merge point
- ❌ History gets noisy with many merge commits
- ❌ Hard to read `git log` on big projects

## Rebase

```
main:    A─B─C
feature:      D'─E'─F'  (replayed on top of C)
```

Replays your commits on top of target. Linear history. Commits get new hashes (D→D').

**Use when:**
- Cleaning up local/private feature branch before PR
- Want linear `git log`
- Keeping feature branch current with main

**Tradeoffs:**
- ✅ Clean, linear history
- ✅ Easy `git bisect` + blame
- ❌ Rewrites history — dangerous on shared branches
- ❌ Multiple conflict rounds (one per replayed commit)
- ❌ Force push required → teammates get confused

## Quick rule

| Situation | Use |
|-----------|-----|
| Merge feature → main | merge |
| Update feature with latest main | rebase |
| Cleaning commits before PR | rebase |
| Shared branch others use | merge |
| Public branch (never rewrite) | merge |

**Golden rule:** Never rebase commits already pushed to shared branch. Rewrites hashes → everyone else branch break.
